svg.title: Iceland, draft exploration map
svg.desc: Top-down concept map for a 1,536 by 1,536 metre driving world. North is up. Landmannalaugar, Langjökull and Kerlingarfjöll form a western highland loop. Kverkfjöll sits on northern Vatnajökull and Lómagnúpur guards its southern approach. Route 1 circles the main island with a separate Westfjords branch. Ódáðahraun spans the Askja-to-Mývatn highland route, and the Skógá runs through Skógafoss to an optional downstream ford and the south sea. The Westfjords are northwest, Surtshellir west-central, Stuðlagil east, Vatnajökull southeast, and the black-sand south coast leads east to Jökulsárlón.
svg.text: 1,536 × 1,536 M · GEOGRAPHY COMPRESSED FOR DRIVING · NORTH UP

path.title: Implemented cairned Vatnajökull through passage; northern connector remains planned.
Western ice cave: winding passage, underground hall and western Y exit to the hillside return. Lakagígar and Askja connections remain planned.
Broad irregular underground ice hall; the complete cave floor is level with the southern clearing.
